vulnerability_analysis: The claimReward() function has a classic reentrancy vulnerability. It transfers BNB to msg.sender via payable(msg.sender).transfer(userShare) BEFORE updating UserrewardPoolOnLastClaim[msg.sender]=_rewardPool. This allows an attacker to re-enter claimReward() multiple times in a single transaction, claiming rewards repeatedly before the state variable is updated. The _rewardPool accumulates BNB from swapAndLiquify operations, and each reentrant call can drain it.
attack_strategy: Deploy a malicious attacker contract with a receive() fallback that calls claimReward() when it receives ETH. The test will: 1) Set up the target contract with owner privileges, 2) Enable swapAndLiquify and accumulate rewards, 3) Transfer MVK tokens to attacker contract, 4) Call claimReward() from attacker which triggers receive() to re-enter claimReward() multiple times, 5) Drain BNB from the reward pool.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Create MaliciousAttacker contract with receive() that re-enters claimReward(). 2. In setUp: Deploy attacker, inject MVK tokens to attacker using deal(), prank as owner to enable swapAndLiquify, ensure target has BNB balance. 3. In testExploit: Record initial BNB balance, call attacker.attack() which triggers claimReward() and reentrancy, assert final balance > initial balance.
